overall: Commission violated the OML by failing to respond within 10 days to a minutes request and by inaccurately recording a motion in its November 29 minutes; all other allegations were rejected.

allegations.summary: Commission argued the December 19, 2018 complaint was untimely because the challenged events occurred at the November 8 open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: In this case, however, the Complainant alleges that the draft notice is evidence that the Chair anticipated that the Sewer Project would be discussed at the November 8 meeting.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the November 8 notice was insufficient because it omitted the Sewer Project, an anticipated topic of discussion.
allegations.key_passage: We find no evidence that the Chair anticipated discussing the Sewer Project at the November 8 meeting, other than in the context of reviewing minutes of the October 18 meeting, which topic was properly included on the November 8 meeting notice.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission discussed the Sewer Project at the November 8 meeting although it was not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Commission did not violate the Law when a discussion of the Sewer Project arose out of a review of the October 18 meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission created and hid an alternative notice listing the Sewer Project item, which was not posted publicly.
allegations.key_passage: In the absence of evidence showing that the Chair anticipated that a discussion of the Sewer Project would take place, we countenance the Commission’s account that the topic was not anticipated by the Chair.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged Commission staff gave false information, including a misrepresentation that the Sewer Project was not discussed at the November 8 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Commission did not violate the Open Meeting Law in the other ways alleged.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Commission failed to respond within 10 days to a November 12 request for November 8 draft minutes.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, the Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely respond to a request for meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the November 8 minutes were inaccurate due to omissions and a slanted summary, including two quoted statements.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Commission’s November 8 meeting minutes substantially comply with the requirement that they provide an accurate and sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion at issue.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the November 29 minutes were generally inaccurate, incomplete, slanted, and included extraneous language.
allegations.key_passage: We find the November 29 meeting minutes to generally be an accurate and detailed account of the discussion that took place.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the November 29 minutes misrecorded the language of Commissioner Murphy's motion, changing its meaning.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Commission’s November 29 meeting minutes are insufficient as to the recording of Commissioner Murphy’s motion, and we order the Commission to amend its minutes to accurately reflect the language of Commissioner Murphy’s motion.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
Amend the November 29 minutes to accurately reflect the language of Commissioner Murphy's motion and certify to the AG's office within 30 days of receipt of the letter.
remedy_passage: we order the Commission to amend its November 29 minutes to accurately reflect the language of Commissioner Murphy’s motion and to certify to our office that it has done so within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter.
